newsitem.title: UK: UK's Sears to sell Freemans to Littlewoods.
newsitem.headline: UK's Sears to sell Freemans to Littlewoods.

text.p: British retailer Sears Plc said on Monday it had signed a conditional agreement to sell its agency mail order business, Freemans, to Littlewoods Organisation for 395 million pounds ($663.8 million) in cash. Sears also said it was developing a structure to return about 410 million pounds in cash to ordinary shareholders in some six months' time.
The company expected to give further details in April of its plan to return cash to shareholders.
After the disposal, the company said it expected savings in central costs of about 4.0 million stg per year.

Sears also said it would look for a buyer or joint venture partner for its home decorations store concept, The Source, resulting in the elimination of about 3.0 million pounds per year of development costs.
Among its other divisions, Sears said the trading performance of its footwear business over the next 12 months would be crucial in terms of determining its potential.
The company said the business's performance had declined versus the prior year, adding that expected benefits from recent changes at the division had yet to materialise.
The company said it expected improved performance at its Selfridges and Sears Clothing businesses to continue.
